clue.text: Praiseworthy lord said to be clever

indicators.note: said tells us the word lord counts for how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: lord and laud are pronounced alike in standard British speech
able means skilful or clever

explanation.surface: A nobleman is admired because people say he is clever.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British English, lord and laud sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of praise deserves to be lauded, a direct synonym.

clue.text: If removed from the affair, can become distant

indicators.note: removed from says one word's letters are taken out of the other word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these two letters are the ones taken out

explanation.surface: A conditional word, dropped from an affair, makes it feel distant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take an I and an F out of AFFAIR and AFAR is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, so as an adjective-like adverb it matches distant.

clue.text: Cleaned up the residue inside a day

indicators.note: inside places the residue within the word for a day

parts.note: WED is the short form of Wednesday
ash is the residue left by burning

explanation.surface: Someone spent a day clearing up leftover mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to clean it, so washed is a plain synonym of cleaned up.

clue.text: Flew across to get a kind of milk

definitions.meaning: first meaning: passed lightly and quickly over a surface
second meaning: milk with the cream taken off

explanation.surface: Someone dashed over to fetch a particular carton of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird or stone that skims glides just over a surface; skimmed milk has had its cream removed.

clue.text: Wise man interrupted by a bishop, one in the union

indicators.note: interrupted by means the wise man's word is broken open and other letters set in its middle

parts.note: a mage is a learned man or magician
taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sage is joined by a bishop to celebrate one couple's wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: RR, for Right Reverend, is a standard crossword abbreviation for a bishop; the inserted letters split the wise man after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is the legal union of two people, a standard synonym.

clue.text: I left out subsidies on free trade

indicators.note: free suggests letters let loose to settle in a new order
left out tells us a letter is dropped from what follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; this is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A government drops subsidies in favour of free trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Is in subsidies goes; the rest, with ON, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade with someone is to do business with them, a verb phrase meaning the same thing.

clue.text: Quarter of a pint that is for Scottish guide

parts.note: a gill is a liquid measure, a quarter of a pint
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A small measure of drink is handed to a Highland guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a man who attends a hunting or fishing party in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Partially returned from a position on the field

parts.note: half means partly, as in half done
back means returned, as in he is back

explanation.surface: A player came partway back from where they were placed on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, rugby and hockey a halfback plays between the forwards and the backs.

clue.text: A teacher is like a god!

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun: Adonis is a godlike young man

parts.note: taken as written
a don is a university teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student gushes that their lecturer is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite, and his name is used for a godlike handsome man.

clue.text: Flower poem read first

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: first keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of read

explanation.surface: A poem about a bloom is to be read before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower in crosswords is often a river, something that flows; the Oder runs along the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river, and a river is something that flows, the crossword-only sense of flower.

clue.text: Entertaining lottery drawn in a funny way

parts.note: amusing or entertaining

indicators.note: drawn as in hung, drawn and quartered means disembowelled, so the inside of the word goes

parts.note: the first and last letters of lottery, with its middle gone

explanation.surface: A lottery draw is presented as comic entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like a lottery draw, but it means gutted: only the outer letters of lottery stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously is the adverb for acting in an amusing manner, a direct synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Mariner on the way to foreign parts

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A sailor sets off on the road to distant lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Going abroad means travelling to another country, the same adverbial idea.

clue.text: Girl, inexperienced, is put in the shade

parts.note: Olive is a girl's name
green means new to something, untried

explanation.surface: A naive young woman is outshone by others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the shade' is an idiom for outclassed, but shade here is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive green is a dull yellowish-green colour, and a shade is a particular tone of colour.

clue.text: Inspector used to be a junior, reportedly

parts.note: ex means former
taken as written

indicators.note: reportedly means the word junior should be rendered by its sound only

parts.note: a minor is a young person; it sounds like a coal miner

explanation.surface: An official inspector admits to having once been a junior.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner scrutinises or inspects things, such as candidates or accounts, closely matching inspector.

clue.text: Claimed to be about the treatment of patients

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective meaning to do with such treatment

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and moved into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is claimed to concern how patients are cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical describes anything relating to medicine, the science and practice of healing the sick.

clue.text: Intimidate a very noisy group of politicians

parts.note: taken as written
ff is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud
the right is the conservative wing of politics

explanation.surface: A loud political faction bullies people.
explanation.definitionFit: Affright is an old word meaning to frighten or scare, close in sense to intimidating.

clue.text: Imitate Old Nick? It's causing difficulty

definitions.note: a participle phrase for a verb meaning to cause difficulty

parts.note: to be a character is to play or imitate it
Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil

explanation.surface: Acting like Satan is said to create trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or plague, persistently creating problems for someone.

clue.text: Dire pint disconcerted the brave

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A terrible pint of beer upset even the bold drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold, a straightforward synonym for courageous.

clue.text: Bolted before winged half could fly

definitions.note: a verb phrase for an adjective meaning able to fly

parts.note: bolted means ran away

indicators.note: half keeps only part of the word before it, here its back portion

parts.note: the last three of its six letters

explanation.surface: A bird bolted before its wings were strong enough to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fledged bird has grown its feathers and is ready to take to the air.

clue.text: Happy when flu outbreak followed salute?

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of greeting or salute

indicators.note: an outbreak bursts things apart, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly merry when an epidemic follows a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful means in good spirits, a plain synonym of glad or content.

clue.text: Marie Antoinette, as she used to be, in confrontation

definitions.text: Marie Antoinette, as she used to be
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French queen before the guillotine still had her skull attached
second meaning: meeting face to face, directly opposed

explanation.surface: The executed queen is recalled, as she was, facing her accusers.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Antoinette was beheaded in 1793, so before then her head was still in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on collision or clash is one where two sides meet face to face directly.

clue.text: Foreign currency provided for English tapes to be translated

indicators.note: translated suggests changing form, so the letters are converted into another arrangement

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money is paid so English recordings can be put into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the monetary unit of Spain before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Trod on paws that were protected

definitions.meaning: first meaning: walked softly on cushioned feet
second meaning: cushioned with soft lining

explanation.surface: Someone stepped on an animal's feet that had some protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat padded across the floor on soft feet; padded clothing is protected by layers of stuffing.

clue.text: Justly thought to have a preference for blondes?

definitions.note: an adverb phrase for an adjective meaning thinking justly
definitions.meaning: first meaning: impartial and just in judgement

definitions.text: to have a preference for blondes
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: having one's mind on light-haired people

explanation.surface: Someone is deemed just, though rumoured to favour blondes.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair means light-haired as well as just, so the second reading is a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair-minded person judges impartially and justly, without prejudice or bias.

clue.text: Chanticleer, maybe, cried for sailors

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a cockerel did, the past tense of its call
second meaning: the people who work a ship

explanation.surface: A rooster called out for the men at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanticleer is the cockerel in Chaucer's tale; a cock crows, and in the past tense it crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company of seamen is its crew; crew is also the old past tense of crow.

clue.text: Implicit yardstick holding definition of a conurbation

indicators.note: holding means the two words together contain the letters needed

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An unstated standard holds a definition of a sprawling urban area.
explanation.definitionFit: A conurbation is a large built-up urban area, which is what a city essentially is.

clue.text: Man, a Spaniard, on empty pitch

parts.note: Jose is a common Spanish man's name

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the next word is removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of pitch, with its middle gone

explanation.surface: A Spanish man stands on a deserted playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph is a man's name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Shocking vote for Richard, hard to take!

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone in

indicators.note: to take means these letters are removed from the name just before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: Voting for a man called Richard is hard to stomach, which is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current gives shocks, and electric also means thrilling or startling, like shocking.
